detail: F(beta)=max over ordered witness pairs of (df - beta dg) equals max_w r_w - min_w r_w for r=f-beta g, so it is a valid lower bound on sup r - inf r over the support for that beta (witnesses are in-support points). F is convex piecewise linear and coercive (pieces come in +/- pairs and some dg != 0), so its minimum lies at a pairwise-equality breakpoint; candidate set (all pairwise intersections plus 0) is complete. Independent exact-rational recomputation from the JSON witness values reproduces every reported value; the minimum is at beta=0 for all five controls in both cases (C3a: dg=0 on the jump pair; others: the jump pair rises for beta>0, the w_hi/w_zero or w_low pair rises for beta<0).

detail: Logic is valid: (i) per beta cell each witness term mu - r_w and r_w - mu is affine in beta, so max_w min(endpoints) lower-bounds the cell minimum of max_w, and the product of the two positive lower bounds lower-bounds the product; (ii) for |beta|>20 the retained witnesses have positive slope in |beta|, so their values at 20 are lower bounds; (iii) over the mean range the product (a+t)(b-t) is concave where positive, so the endpoints of [price-L1, price+L1] are the worst case. An independent exact evaluation (1e-4 grid on [-30,30], all kinks, tails to 1e6) gives sup gains 1.59284 (C3b), 1.14919 (C3a), 1.01529 (C1/C2a/C2b) at B8x52, each just below the reported 1.5933/1.1498/1.0158, as an upper bound should be; no beta is missed. Minor points: (a) the mean range price +- L1 is assumed, not derived in the script (fine as assm). (b) The U1 gain is modelled as sqrt(m_b(S-m_b))/sqrt(m(S_res-m)), i.e. the U1 call count is taken as proportional to sqrt(m(S-m)). The k_bracket rows show it is not: at fixed span the U1 credit moves k only 352.97 -> 197.60 (x1.786) while sqrt(m(S-m))/S would predict x3.57, so an S-proportional term remains. Under a two-term cost a*sqrt(m(S-m)) + b*S, the true gain lies between gain_U1 and gain_linear, so the probe headline max(gain_linear, gain_U1) (2.49 for F04 h) is the right q+ ceiling, while the JSON M_after values (which use min(v/gu, v*1.786/gl), i.e. a 1.70 factor) may understate the gain. The kill threshold should therefore be applied to max(gl, gu), as the verdict does; this makes any route with S_res <= 9.7 (gl >= 4) unresolved by this metric (see check 5).

detail: (i) Lower bound: own PCA (basis.py closed forms) matches the probe factor exactly; y_hi has max|y|=4.6458 <= 4.7; h(y_hi) by direct midpoint quadrature of the PATHWISE knock-out payoff along the line (no root solve, no closed form, 36000 nodes on [-9,9]) = 15.62347, equal to the closed form and above the certified 15.6124. Confirmed. (ii) Upper bound: first PCA loading is exactly constant across assets within a date (spread 0.0, all v>0), so basket_j(z)=basket_j(z_H)e^{v_j(z-z_H)} <= H e^{-v_j(z_H-z)} for z<z_H and knocked out above z_H; h(y) <= h*(z_H(y)) is valid; the maximisation over a 0.01 z_H grid is not interval-certified but the max is interior (0.84) so the grid error is O(1e-4). (iii) Universal monotone bound reproduced (11.4232 B8x52, 11.0070 B4x12). The argument (profile all log prices at ln H at z*, Jensen per date, |v_c| <= sigma sqrt(t_j)) is right but needs nonnegative loadings and an unclamped support, as labelled. (iv) It does NOT cover non-monotone directions. A sign-free construction (x_c(z*) = ln H - |v_c| w, alive for |z-z*|<w) gives sup h >= 7.66 (B8x52) / 7.37 (B4x12) for ANY direction, unclamped, i.e. a linear gain up to 5.07 is not excluded by the probe for non-monotone directions; under the probe ceiling metric max(gl, gu) that is not excluded by theory. In practice explicit mixed-sign directions are far worse: integrating PCA column 1 or 7 (asset-Helmert, mixed signs) leaves an in-box witness with h >= 37.1 / 36.9 (pathwise quadrature, max|y| 2.30), i.e. no span reduction at all; the PCA-first direction is the relevant one. (v) The h-span witness has Euclidean norm ||y_hi||=48.1 in 415 dims: inside the box but with negligible probability (see check 5).

detail: The desk ratio 3.61 for coherent preintegration is not well supported. desk_deff costs the classical kernel generically: 3 Newton iterations with one exp per coordinate for the strike root AND for 52 barrier roots (2496 exps), plus 416 exps and 834 normal CDFs for the closed form. But the first PCA loading is constant across assets within a date (verified: spread 0.0; the probe itself uses this for its upper bound). Hence S_j = sum_i e^{a_ij} once (the 416 exps replace the baseline e^{x_c}, zero extra), every barrier root is closed form z_j = (ln(na H) - ln S_j)/v_j (52 ln, no Newton), the strike root is a Newton solve over 52 terms (52 exps per iteration), and the closed form needs 2(nt+1)=106 CDFs, not 834. Structure-aware count at the floor-sheet polynomial costs: extra ~1.09e7 Toffoli (3 iters) to 2.07e7 (8 iters), D ratio 1.23-1.44, versus the probe 1.22e8 / 3.61. Not counted by the probe (q-): the loader change from the one-factor prefix-sum model to PCA coordinates; a naive dense time transform is ~5.6e7 Toffoli (ratio +1.2), a fast DST or a direction native to the one-factor loader is much cheaper. So a defensible range is ~1.2-2.4, not 3.6, and the after-cost figure (0.69 in STATUS) should read ~0.7-1.4 on the consistent gain 1.70. The kill itself does not depend on D: at D ratio 1 the best evaluated route is 2.49 in the probe metric and 1.70 consistently, both < 4, so the D=1 claim holds for the evaluated (1-D, single-control) routes. It does not hold for preintegration in general: integrating k>1 directions coherently drives the span toward 0 (k=d is computing the price), so a D=1 kill cannot cover multi-dimensional preintegration; that route needs its own cost argument (in-oracle quadrature with Q nodes per extra direction multiplies D by >= Q).
evidence: Floor sheet B8x52 primary_n72: compute_toffolis 46,868,770; per exp 32,017; per ln-class poly 29,247. Probe extra 122,211,832 -> 3.6075. Structure-aware: 10,898,036 (3 iters) -> 1.233; 20,742,451 (8 iters) -> 1.443. Dense PCA time transform 56,070,144 -> +1.196.
suggested_fix: Recount pre_h_replacement with the per-date structure (52 closed-form barrier roots, 52-term strike Newton, 106 CDFs) and add the loader-transform cost; report a range (~1.2-2.4). Scope the D=1 kill sentence to one-dimensional preintegration and the listed controls, and add a cost argument for k>1 preintegration.

detail: (a) Multi-control / any finite combination of controls continuous at the arithmetic barrier: covered by the jump argument (check 2), S_res >= ~38.6. (b) Controls carrying the same all-date arithmetic-basket barrier need the joint law of arithmetic basket maxima; no certifiable mean cheaper than pricing f; excluded. (c) Piecewise/conditional beta is just another control; IS/change of measure raises the worst-case span (likelihood ratio grows at support corners where f is still ~38.6); antithetic or sign-flip symmetrisation costs >= 2x per flip and h(-y_hi)=6.33 keeps the symmetrised sup >= 10.98. (d) Euclidean-ball truncation of the support (bias <= 17.3*P(|y|>R): 6.6e-5 at R=24): the h witness y_hi has ||y||=48, but a hill-climb finds h >= 13.62 at ||y||=23.97 and h >= 14.51 at R=26, so gl <= 2.85; no help. (e) Raw-f layering/clipping: tail of f is heavy, best 2-layer U1 gain 1.30. (f) NOT covered, and it breaks the kill at D ratio 1: CLIPPED preintegration. sup h = 15.6 is reached only at box corners; the distribution of h is light-tailed (20,000 random y: mean 3.275, sd 1.151, q.99 5.74, q.999 6.40, max 7.18; E[(h-7)^+] ~ 9e-6, E[(h-6)^+] ~ 1.1e-3, E[(h-5.55)^+] ~ 5.3e-3). Encoding min(h, tau) (span tau) and estimating (h-tau)^+ separately (classically: tiny variance; or as a second quantum layer whose U1 cost is ~sqrt(m2*Delta2) with m2 ~ 1e-5..5e-3) gives, with the probe own formulas: tau=7: gl=5.55, gu=3.11 -> probe ceiling metric max(gl,gu)=5.55 >= 4 (not killed); consistent pairing ~3.1. tau=5.55 (classical tail 5.3e-3, sd ~0.04, a few thousand classical paths): gl=7.0, gu~3.98, consistent pairing ~3.9-4.0. A fully quantum 2-layer split of h (cut 7.3, exact layer means, linear error split) gives 2.99 on the sqrt term. So at D ratio 1 a clipped/hybrid preintegration route reaches ~3.1-7 depending on the metric and on the classical tail allowance; only after charging D_res/D (>= ~1.2, check 6) and the classical tail cost does it drop below 4 (e.g. 3.98/1.23 = 3.2). (g) k>1-dimensional preintegration (span -> 0 as k -> d) is out of a D=1 kill by construction; needs a cost argument. Bias of clipping is MC-estimated, not certified; certifying a 1e-4 tail bound is itself nontrivial, which is the natural place to close (f).
